summary: Add-my-Pet holds raw literature-transcribed age–length and age–weight series (tL/tW data blocks with units and bibkeys) per species across animal phyla, openly served as mydata_*.m files; this covers the size-at-age variable across long- and short-lived taxa, with AnAge (4,671 species, dataset.zip 169 KB) supplying maximum longevity for the long-/short-lived split. FishBase gives only fitted von Bertalanffy parameters, which cannot show an early slow phase. Coverage of the earliest and latest ages varies entry by entry and the raw data must be parsed out of MATLAB files.
next_step: Parse tL/tW blocks from all AmP mydata files into one table (species, age, size, source), join AnAge longevity, then pre-register the test for position of maximum growth velocity and terminal slowdown per species.
obstacles_confirmed: Von Bertalanffy fits force the maximum growth rate to the origin and can hide an early slow start.
Comparable raw longitudinal growth curves are scattered.
